evals.name: default-48h-full-workflow
evals.expected_output: Discovers files changed in the last 48h, groups them by ecosystem/project, runs a simplifier agent on each group, reports per-group results and final verification.
expectations: Runs git log to discover changed files
Filters out non-code files (.md, .lock, data files)
Verifies files exist on disk
Groups files by project/ecosystem relatedness
Orders groups by dependency (config first, tests last)
Creates tasks for each group
Runs a simplifier agent per group
Runs ecosystem-appropriate verification after each group
Presents the final summary table

evals.name: time-window-argument
evals.expected_output: Same workflow but scans 7 days of git history instead of the default 48h, normalizing the shorthand for git's approxidate parser.
expectations: Parses '7d' as the time window argument
Normalizes the shorthand to '7 days' before passing it to git log --since
Handles a larger file count gracefully (may produce more groups)

evals.name: natural-language-trigger
evals.prompt: I've been working on a bunch of stuff over the past few days and forgot to run simplify after each task. Can you clean everything up?
evals.expected_output: Triggers the batch-simplify skill automatically from natural language and runs the full workflow with the default window.
expectations: Skill triggers from natural language (not slash command)
Uses the default 48h time window
Produces the same grouped simplification workflow

evals.name: deferred-items-never-dropped
evals.expected_output: Branch-mode run where simplifier agents report deferred items; the skill consolidates them, presents them grouped by priority, and files work items rather than dropping them.
expectations: Extracts each agent's ## Deferred section verbatim rather than paraphrasing
Consolidates duplicate cross-group concerns into single items
Presents the consolidated deferred list to the user grouped by priority
Files work items for actionable deferred concerns (tracker plugin, gh issue create, or explicit user presentation)

evals.name: argument-parsing-is-token-exact
evals.expected_output: Does not route to branch mode. 'rebranch' merely contains the substring 'branch'; it equals no branch trigger phrase and matches no time-window pattern, so the skill asks the user what was meant rather than guessing.
expectations: Does NOT treat 'rebranch' as a branch-mode request (substring containment is not a match)
Does not silently fall back to the 48h default for an argument it cannot classify
Asks the user what scope was intended, per the detection heuristic's unknown-argument rule
The docs flag is stripped token-wise: a token is dropped only when it equals 'docs', so an argument containing those letters is left intact for the mode parser

evals.name: repo-mode-gates-on-a-confirmed-inventory
evals.expected_output: Enters repo mode, discovers the whole-repository file universe, refuses to start if the sweep universe carries tracked modifications, and presents an inventory summary for confirmation before dispatching any simplifier agent.
expectations: Routes 'repo' to repo mode rather than the 48h default or the ask-the-user rule
Discovers files with git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard anchored to the repository root, not a time-window or branch diff
Checks for tracked modifications in the sweep universe only, and does not refuse on the basis of the working-notes location
Presents an inventory summary — file count, group count, wave plan, scale estimate, exclusions by class — and waits for confirmation before spawning any simplifier
Does NOT dispatch simplifier agents before the user confirms
Loads context/repo-mode.md for the repo-scale machinery rather than improvising it

evals.name: empty-scan-offers-repo-mode-without-escalating
evals.expected_output: Finds no changed code files in the window, reports that, and names repo mode as an option the user may choose. It does not widen its own scope.
expectations: Reports that no code files changed in the 24h window and exits
Names /code-tidying:batch-simplify repo as an available next step in that same report
Does NOT begin a whole-repository sweep on its own — offering is not entering
Waits for the user to ask before any repo-mode work starts

evals.name: repo-mode-verifies-and-files-per-its-own-doctrine
evals.prompt: I reviewed the inventory summary you just presented for the repo-mode run. It looks right — go ahead and run it.
evals.expected_output: Treats the reply as the confirmation the gate was waiting on and proceeds with the planned run: each group through a simplifier and then a fresh-context refutation verifier, one pull request per wave, work items filed for High-priority deferrals only while every deferral is persisted to the run-state inventory.
expectations: Proceeds from the already-presented inventory rather than re-discovering or re-planning the run
Runs a fresh-context verifier per group that tries to refute 'behavior preserved' — mandatory in repo mode, not optional as in the diff-scoped modes
Does NOT treat the end-of-run cross-ecosystem pass as sufficient on its own at repo scale
Reports groups with no mapped test suite as unmapped rather than as passing
Persists every deferred item to the run-state inventory at the consuming project's working-notes location, never a hardcoded path
Files work items for High-priority deferrals only, with no numeric cap, one item per concern rather than per site
Delivers one independently mergeable pull request per wave, merged before the next wave opens — not one repository-wide pull request
Keeps concurrency to a 4-6 simplifier soft cap and degrades to sequential under rate-limit pressure rather than retrying
